cases.name: Kara Rayleen Sanders Taylor
cases.about:
Described as a “phenomenal mom,” Taylor leaves behind a 22-year-old special needs daughter. “Kara was a very loving and caring person who would do anything for anyone if she knew it would make a day in their life better. She was trusting and had faith in others and believed there was good in everyone,” Taylor’s family said in a statement released by the Oregon City Police Department.

Taylor’s husband and brother (Marcus Sanders) described her as a helpful, joyful and selfless woman. When Sanders’ 16-month-old child died from a seizure in 2005, Taylor spent more than a month cooking and shopping for her brother and sister-in-law, to make their lives just a little bit easier while they grieved.

She laughed “all the time” and loved to tell jokes and stories.

“She loved togetherness,” Sanders said. “She loved spending time with people.”

Taylor was a traveling respiratory therapist and was working at a Hermiston hospital when she met her husband Dennis Taylor during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. They worked together for months, trying to keep people alive. They started dating and, six months after they met, Dennis Taylor proposed. Dennis Taylor said he was particularly impressed, and touched, to see how devoted Kara Taylor was to her daughter, Nicole Wood. He said Wood, 22, has severe autism, cannot speak and requires 24-hour one-on-one care.

But Dennis and Kara Taylor’s marriage soon broke down, in part because of Kara Taylor’s struggles with drug and alcohol addiction, Dennis Taylor claimed in court. Dennis Taylor filed for a divorce and a restraining order against her in June, less than a year after they married.

“At times, Kara struggled to find an inner sense of worth and belonging,” Dennis Taylor said. “And then when we separated, it was hard on both of us.”

Kara Taylor moved out of their Pasco, Washington, home in June, and in the months that followed moved among friends’ houses in Oregon.

Her obituary said, "Kara spent her younger years in the Bellingham area before moving to Dallas, Oregon where she attended public schools. In 2000, Kara was blessed to become a mother to a beautiful daughter named Nicole. Nicole suffers from severe Autism and Kara considered every moment that she got to spend with Nicole to be a blessing from God. Kara was the kind of person that looked at every day as an opportunity to try and help somebody less fortunate than her, even if only for a moment. Kara had a heart of gold and considered everyone she met to be a friend.

Kara had a desire to make a difference in the lives of more people, so she attended the Pima Medical Institute in Renton, WA, graduating in 2013 with a degree in Respiratory Therapy. She continued her education through Grand Canyon University, earning a Baccalaureate degree, graduating summa cum laude in 2016. Kara was a member of the Alpha Chi National Honor Society, the Lambda Beta National Honor Society for the profession of Respiratory Care and went on to achieve certification as a Registered Respiratory Therapist, excelling in her chosen profession. Kara worked for many years in hospitals throughout the West Coast. During the Covid-19 pandemic, Kara worked as a traveling Respiratory Therapist, placing the lives of complete strangers before her own by setting up FEMA-operated COVID-19 camps in some of the hardest hit areas of California, before eventually ending up at Good Shepherd Hospital in Hermiston, Oregon where she met her husband, Dennis Taylor. They were married in August 2022 and made their home in Pasco, WA."
cases.narrative: On 8/11/2023 investigators went to the Coffin Butte Landfill in Corvallis, Ore., where they searched for several days, according to an updated Facebook post from the Oregon City Police Department. Authorities eventually discovered human remains believed to be those of Taylor. The Clackamas County Medical Examiner's Office is working to positively identify the remains.  He allegedly dismembered her and discarded parts of her body in different municipal garbage dumps.

cases.name: Jennifer Ruth Stuart
cases.narrative:
On 9/01/2025, her body was eventually discovered in Mount Hood National Forest in Clackamas County after a couple hunting on Forest Service land off Hillockborn Road noted the presence of turkey vultures swarming around an object and saw what appeared to be human remains. Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office investigators used fingerprints to identify the body as that of Stuart. An autopsy determined Stuart died from a gunshot and noted an apparent entry wound in the lower left side of her body.

Blake shot Jennifer at his home on 8/14/2025, then drove to a Home Depot store and purchased a large tote, garbage bags and gloves. Surveillance video from Home Depot and from the area near where Stuart’s body found captured Blake’s vehicle. Blake initially put Stuart’s body in the large tote but later retrieved the tote, fearing it could tie him to the body. Police discovered the tote during a second search of Blake’s property.
